grade.basis: Independent reading of complete 26-page score, sampled at PDF pages 2–3, 6, 10, 15, 18, 20, 22, 25–26 across all four movements. First viola consistently has the highest exposed line, with upper-position melodic writing and chromatic semiquaver figures already in the Andante (quarter=70, e.g. bars 27–33). The long second movement (Allegro quarter=130, 3/8) asks for sustained rhythmic accuracy, repeated semiquavers, clean chromatic changes, register/clef changes and occasional pizzicato/arco coordination, rather than extreme left-hand virtuosity. Lento (quarter=55) adds expressive sustained upper-register playing, ornaments and rapid ornamental runs (e.g. bar 47). Vivo (quarter=130) requires continuous semiquaver stamina in supporting parts, increasingly active upper lines, string-crossing figures, and explicit ricochet triplets in viola 1 near bars 73–74, with a final rapid chromatic ascent. These combined whole-work demands fit pre-diploma level 6: more sustained bow control and positional fluency than an ordinary grade-8 chamber piece, but sampled notation does not support professional-level virtuosity. Approximately 18-minute four-movement scope corroborated by primary metadata and premiere metadata. Ensemble balance, independent entries and shared articulation matter, but no automatic extra ensemble level is applied. Representative reading supports the estimate within about one level; not a bar-by-bar audit.

findings.finding: Cached primary page 1223973 identifies the original four-viola quartet in D minor, four movements, approximately 18 minutes, with complete score and all four individual parts. Complete local score was read directly; score movement headings are Andante quarter=70, Allegro quarter=130, Lento quarter=55 and Vivo quarter=130.
